title: SASA 1: The SGB and the principal
description: Who sits on a school governing body, what it must and may do under the South African Schools Act, and how it works with the principal.

lessons.title: What an SGB is and who sits on it
lessons.summary: Governance versus management, the members of an SGB, the parent majority and terms of office.
lessons.body:
## 🏛️ Governance and management are different jobs

The South African Schools Act 84 of 1996 (SASA) splits the running of a public school into two jobs. **Governance** of every public school is vested in its governing body (SASA s16(1)). **Professional management**, the day to day running of teaching and staff, is done by the principal under the authority of the Head of Department (HOD) of the provincial education department (SASA s16(3)).

SASA s16(2) adds that a governing body stands in a **position of trust** towards the school. That means members must act honestly, in good faith and in the interests of the school, not in their own interests or those of a friend or a business.

> 💡 Tip: Most of this module is about public schools. An independent school is usually run by a board of governors under its own constitution, so check which SASA sections your registration conditions and provincial law apply to you. When we speak generally we say "SGB or board of governors".

## 👪 Who sits on the SGB of an ordinary public school

SASA s23(1) and (2) list the members:

- **Elected members**: parents of learners at the school, educators at the school, non-educator staff, and learners in grade 8 or higher (s23(2)).
- **The principal**, as an ex officio member, in other words a member because of the post (s23(1)(b)).
- **Co-opted members**, if the SGB chooses to add them (s23(6)).

A parent who is employed at the school may not represent parents on the SGB (s23(3)). The learner members are elected by the representative council of learners (s23(4)).

### ⚖️ The parent majority

SASA s23(9) says the number of parent members must be **one more than the combined total of the other members who have voting rights**. Count every other voting member, including the principal, then add one. Example: a high school with the principal, three educators, one non-educator and three learners has eight other voting members, so it needs at least nine parent members.

Co-opted members do not have voting rights (s23(8)), so they are not counted.

## 🗳️ Elections and term of office

SASA s31 sets the maximum terms:

1. A member who is not a learner: **not more than three years** (s31(1)).
2. A learner member: **not more than one year** (s31(2)).
3. An office-bearer, such as the chairperson: **not more than one year** (s31(3)), so office-bearers are elected again each year.
4. A member or office-bearer may be re-elected or co-opted after the term ends (s31(4)).

The detailed rules (who runs the election, vacancies, how many members in each category) are set by notice under SASA s28. The BELA Act s22 moved this power from the provincial MEC to the national Minister. Until new national rules replace them, schools follow the election regulations their province issued, so confirm the current notice and the next election date with your district office.

> ⚠️ Watch out: SGB members may not be paid for their work or for attending meetings and school activities (SASA s27(2) as amended by BELA s21). Necessary expenses may be reimbursed (s27(1)).

## ✅ Key points

- Governance belongs to the SGB (s16(1)); professional management belongs to the principal under the HOD (s16(3)).
- Members are parents, educators, non-educator staff, learners in grade 8 and up, plus the principal ex officio (s23).
- Parents must outnumber all other voting members by one (s23(9)).
- Adult members serve up to three years, learner members and office-bearers up to one year (s31).

lessons.title: What the SGB must do and may apply to do
lessons.summary: The functions every SGB has under section 20 and the extra functions it can be allocated under section 21.
lessons.body:
## 📋 Section 20: the functions every SGB has

SASA s20(1) lists what the governing body of every public school **must** do. In plain English:

- **Promote the best interests of the school** and strive for its development through quality education for all learners (s20(1)(a)).
- **Adopt a constitution** for the SGB (s20(1)(b)).
- **Develop the mission statement** of the school (s20(1)(c)).
- **Adopt a code of conduct for learners** (s20(1)(d), read with s8).
- **Support the principal, educators and other staff** in their professional functions (s20(1)(e)).
- **Determine the times of the school day**, in line with staff conditions of employment (s20(1)(f)).
- **Administer and control the school's property**, buildings and grounds, including hostels (s20(1)(g)).
- **Encourage voluntary service** by parents, learners and staff (s20(1)(h)).
- **Recommend appointments** of educators and non-educator staff to the HOD (s20(1)(i) and (j)). The SGB recommends; the department appoints state-paid staff.
- **Allow reasonable use of the facilities** for educational programmes not run by the school, at the HOD's request (s20(1)(k)).
- Carry out all other functions given to it by SASA or by the Minister or MEC by notice (s20(1)(l) and (m)).

SASA s20(2) also lets the SGB allow the reasonable use of school facilities for community, social and fund-raising purposes on reasonable and equitable conditions, which may include charging a fee. Finance details, such as the school fund and budgets, are covered in the School finances modules.

> 💡 Tip: When a parent asks "who decides?", start with s20. If the item is on the list, it is an SGB job. If it is about teaching, timetables for educators or managing staff, it is usually the principal's professional management under s16(3).

## ➕ Section 21: functions the SGB can apply for

Under SASA s21(1) an SGB may apply **in writing** to the HOD to be allocated extra functions:

1. To maintain and improve the school's property, buildings and grounds, including hostels (s21(1)(a)).
2. To determine the extra-mural curriculum and the choice of subject options in terms of provincial curriculum policy (s21(1)(b)).
3. To purchase textbooks, educational materials or equipment (s21(1)(c)).
4. To pay for services to the school (s21(1)(d)).
5. Other functions consistent with SASA and provincial law (s21(1)(e)).

The HOD may refuse only if the SGB does not have the **capacity** to perform the function effectively (s21(2)). The HOD may approve with or without conditions (s21(3)) and must give the decision and reasons in writing (s21(4)). Anyone aggrieved may appeal to the MEC (s21(5)). The MEC may also, by notice, allow some SGBs to perform these functions without applying (s21(6)).

Schools with these functions are often called "section 21 schools". BELA s14 added s21(3A), which lets the HOD, after consulting the SGB, centrally procure identified learning and teaching support material, unless the SGB proves its own supplier is more cost effective.

> ⚠️ Watch out: Allocated functions can be withdrawn by the HOD under SASA s22 if the SGB does not perform them properly. BELA s15 rewrote s22, so check the current procedure before relying on old guidance.

## ✅ Key points

- Section 20 lists the functions every public school SGB must perform, from the mission statement to property and staff recommendations.
- The SGB recommends staff appointments; the department makes them (s20(1)(i) and (j)).
- Section 21 functions must be applied for in writing and may be refused only for lack of capacity (s21(1) and (2)).
- A refused applicant may appeal to the MEC (s21(5)).

lessons.title: The principal: duties and working with the SGB
lessons.summary: What section 16A requires of the principal and how the principal and SGB share the work.
lessons.body:
## 🧑‍🏫 The principal wears two hats

The principal is an employee of the provincial education department and also a member of the SGB. SASA s16A(1)(a) says the principal represents the HOD on the governing body when acting in an official capacity. So in an SGB meeting the principal is both a voting member and the department's representative.

SASA s16A was inserted in 2007 to spell out the principal's duties.

## 📌 The principal's duties under section 16A

### 🏫 Professional management (s16A(2)(a))

The principal must, among other things:

- Implement all educational programmes and curriculum activities.
- Manage all educators and support staff.
- Manage learning support material and other equipment.
- Perform functions delegated by the HOD.
- Safekeep all school records.
- Implement policy and legislation.

### 🤝 Duties towards the SGB

The principal must also:

1. Attend and take part in all SGB meetings (s16A(2)(b)).
2. Report to the SGB on the professional management of the school (s16A(2)(c)).
3. Assist the SGB with learner disciplinary matters (s16A(2)(d)).
4. Inform the SGB about policy and legislation (s16A(2)(f)).
5. Assist the SGB in managing the school's funds, advise it on the financial implications of decisions, take reasonable steps to prevent financial maladministration, serve on the finance committee and report any mismanagement to the SGB and the HOD (s16A(2)(h) to (k)).

The principal must also give the HOD an annual report on academic performance and the use of resources (s16A(1)(b)), and, at a school identified as underperforming, prepare an improvement plan and table it at an SGB meeting (s16A(1)(c)).

> 💡 Tip: s16A(3) says the principal must assist the SGB, but not in a way that conflicts with HOD instructions, legislation or policy, or the principal's duties as an employee. If a principal says "I cannot do that, it conflicts with a departmental instruction", ask to see the instruction rather than forcing the issue.

## ⚖️ Making the relationship work

The SGB governs and sets policy. The principal manages and implements. A good rule of thumb:

- The SGB decides **what** the school's policies say (for example the code of conduct or admission policy).
- The principal and staff decide **how** to apply them every day.

Example: the SGB adopts a homework and attendance rule in the code of conduct. The principal decides which educator follows up absences and how registers are checked. The SGB does not instruct individual educators; it raises concerns through the principal.

The SGB must support the principal and staff in their professional functions (s20(1)(e)). In return, the principal must keep the SGB informed and attend its meetings (s16A(2)(b) and (c)). Conflict usually starts when one side crosses into the other's lane, for example SGB members giving staff orders, or a principal spending school funds without SGB approval.

> ⚠️ Watch out: Labour matters for state-paid educators are handled by the HOD (s16A(2)(e)), not the SGB. The SGB is the employer only of staff it appoints and pays itself.

## ✅ Key points

- The principal represents the HOD on the SGB (s16A(1)(a)).
- The principal must attend SGB meetings and report on professional management (s16A(2)(b) and (c)).
- The principal assists with learner discipline and school funds and must report financial mismanagement (s16A(2)(d), (h) to (k)).
- The SGB governs and sets policy; the principal manages and implements (s16).

lessons.title: Meetings, committees and co-opted members
lessons.summary: How often the SGB must meet, how committees work, who can be co-opted and when members must declare interests.
lessons.body:
## 🗓️ The constitution and meetings

Every public school SGB must function under a **constitution** that meets the minimum requirements set by the MEC (SASA s18(1)). The SGB must send a copy to the HOD within 90 days of its election (s18(3)).

SASA s18(2) says the constitution must provide for:

1. A meeting of the SGB **at least once every school term** (s18(2)(a)).
2. Meetings of the SGB with parents, learners, educators and other staff, each **at least once a year** (s18(2)(b)).
3. **Recording and keeping minutes** of SGB meetings (s18(2)(c)).
4. Making the minutes **available for inspection by the HOD** (s18(2)(d)).
5. A **report on its activities** to parents, learners, educators and staff at least once a year (s18(2)(e)).

Quorums, notice periods and voting rules are set in your SGB constitution and provincial rules, so check those documents rather than assuming a number.

> 💡 Tip: Keep a simple year planner: four SGB meetings (one per term), the annual parents meeting, and the yearly meetings with learners, educators and staff. Minute every one.

## 🧩 Committees

SASA s30(1) says an SGB may:

- Establish committees, including an executive committee (s30(1)(a)).
- Appoint people who are not SGB members to committees **on grounds of expertise**, but an SGB member must **chair each committee** (s30(1)(b)).

An ordinary public school that teaches learners with special education needs must have a committee on special education needs (s30(2)).

Common committees are finance, discipline, admissions, safety and fundraising. Since BELA s23, SASA s29(2)(b) says that, where reasonably practicable, only a parent member who is not employed at the school may chair the finance committee. The SGB chairperson must always be a parent member not employed at the school (s29(2)(a)).

## 🙋 Co-opted members

SASA s23(6), as substituted by BELA s16, lets the SGB co-opt members of the community, or people from outside the community, **with relevant expertise** to help it perform its functions. Examples: a retired accountant, a building contractor, a lawyer.

- Co-opted members **do not vote** (s23(8)).
- A school serving learners with special needs must, where practically possible, co-opt someone with expertise in those needs (s23(5)).

## 🚫 Declaring interests and recusal

SASA s26, as substituted by BELA s20, now requires a member to **declare any direct or indirect personal and financial interest** before the SGB discusses or decides on the recruitment or employment of staff or the procurement of goods and services. This includes interests of the member's family, close friends and business partners. BELA detail on recusal is covered in the BELA modules.

> ⚠️ Watch out: A member who is a minor may not contract on behalf of the school or vote on resolutions that impose liabilities on the school or third parties (SASA s32(1) and (2)). Plan who signs before the meeting.

## ✅ Key points

- The SGB must meet at least once a term and keep minutes the HOD can inspect (s18(2)).
- The SGB must report on its activities to parents, learners and staff at least once a year (s18(2)(e)).
- Committees may include outside experts, but an SGB member must chair each one (s30(1)(b)).
- Co-opted members bring expertise but have no vote (s23(6) and (8)).
- Members must declare interests before staffing or procurement decisions (s26 as substituted by BELA).

questions.text: Under SASA, in whom is the governance of a public school vested?
questions.explanation: SASA s16(1): the governance of every public school is vested in its governing body. Professional management belongs to the principal under the HOD (s16(3)).

questions.text: A high school SGB has the principal, three educators, one non-educator and three learners as voting members. What is the minimum number of parent members?
questions.explanation: SASA s23(9): parent members must be one more than the combined total of other voting members. 8 other voting members plus one is 9.

questions.text: What is the maximum term of office of a parent member of an SGB?
questions.explanation: SASA s31(1): the term of office of a member other than a learner may not exceed three years.

questions.text: What is the maximum term of office of the SGB chairperson as an office-bearer?
questions.explanation: SASA s31(3): the term of office of an office-bearer may not exceed one year, although he or she may be re-elected (s31(4)).

questions.text: A parent who works as an admin clerk at the school wants to stand as a parent member. What does SASA say?

options.text: She may stand if the principal agrees
She may not represent parents on the SGB
She may stand but may not vote
She may stand only as chairperson

questions.explanation: SASA s23(3): a parent who is employed at the school may not represent parents on the governing body.

questions.text: Which of these is a function every public school SGB must perform under section 20?

options.text: Developing the mission statement of the school

questions.explanation: SASA s20(1)(c): the SGB must develop the mission statement. It only recommends appointments to the HOD (s20(1)(i) and (j)).

questions.text: On what ground may the HOD refuse an SGB application for a section 21 function?

options.text: Only if the SGB lacks the capacity to perform it effectively
Whenever the district prefers to keep the function

questions.explanation: SASA s21(2): the HOD may refuse an application only if the governing body does not have the capacity to perform the function effectively.

questions.text: Which statement about the principal is correct under section 16A?

options.text: The principal may not vote at SGB meetings
The principal attends SGB meetings only when invited
The principal reports only to the SGB chairperson
The principal represents the HOD on the SGB and must attend and take part in its meetings

questions.explanation: SASA s16A(1)(a) and s16A(2)(b): the principal represents the HOD on the SGB in an official capacity and must attend and participate in all SGB meetings.

questions.text: How often must the SGB of a public school meet, at minimum?

options.text: Only when the principal calls a meeting

questions.explanation: SASA s18(2)(a): the SGB constitution must provide for a meeting of the governing body at least once every school term.

questions.text: The SGB co-opts a retired accountant to help the finance committee. Which is true?

options.text: She must chair the finance committee
She has no vote on the SGB
She counts towards the parent majority

questions.explanation: SASA s23(6) as substituted by BELA s16 allows co-opting people with expertise, and s23(8) says co-opted members do not have voting rights. An SGB member must chair each committee (s30(1)(b)).
